text:
alexa: heads up — west-south2 dedicated cluster showing allocatable drop, several GPU nodes flapping since 11:42 UTC. we have a pile of pending gpu pods. thinking about routing low-priority traffic to hosted as a temporary spillover. cc @sre-oncall
infra-bot: ALERT: Dedicated GPU pool west-south2 health degraded (node-flap). 11:44 UTC. IncidentID: gpu-ws2-2191
raj: seeing the same. scheduler queue: ~80% gpu-request pending. autoscaler log shows repeated failures to provision. snippet: `Scale loop: insufficient capacity for resource gpu: requested 12, available 0`
maria: any failed mounts or kubelet errors? could be transient network peering issue.
ben: checked node logs — kubelet restarted 3x on each affected host, plus control-plane RTT spikes. peering maintenance looks likely from provider side.
alexa: plan: 1) shift low-priority dev traffic to hosted (30%) to relieve backlog 2) cordon+drain obviously flaky nodes 3) triage autoscaler not scaling. who can flip the routing weight?
raj: I can flip weights. running: `rbacctl set-weight pool:west-south2-hosted 0.3 --reason "spillover due to node flap"`
infra-bot: Routing change applied by raj at 11:50 UTC — hosted weight +30% — :white_check_mark:
sre-oncall: hold up — billing alert fired for hosted at 11:51 (cost burn spike). we should ensure we only route dev/test orgs. tagging cost-team.
maria: agree. we should limit overflow selector to org:dev and org:staging only, not prod orgs. raj, can you update selector?
raj: updated overflow selector: `--selector "org in (dev,staging)"` — applied at 11:52 UTC. currently routing only 8 orgs. p95 for prod unchanged.
ben: cordoning node gpu-ws2-17 and draining now: `kubectl cordon gpu-ws2-17 && kubectl drain gpu-ws2-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
ben: autoscaler log extract: ```[11:53:02] autoscaler: scale_decision suppressed due to control-plane-rtt=12.3s
[11:53:03] aws-provisioner: send request failed: peering-timeout
[11:53:05] autoscaler: retrying scale after jitter```
infra-bot: Metric update: dedicated GPU utilization dropped 98% -> 72% after routing change (11:56 UTC). queued pending pods decreased from 124 -> 18.
sre-oncall: monitoring for 15m. Ben, open an incident in incidents channel and add cost owner.
ben: Created INC-2024-892 in #incidents with initial timeline and cost-owner tag. link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2024-892
maria: FYI the autoscaler PR is queued — root cause: race when control-plane RTT > 10s causing a short-circuit. I'll pick this up and push a hotfix.
alexa: thanks. once autoscaler is stable and nodes healthy we'll revert routing weights. I'll draft a short customer note for any degraded calls (brief, technical).
infra-bot: Follow-up metrics will be posted to the runbooks channel. Recommend keeping overflow active until autoscaler fix and peering cleared.
sre-oncall: acknowledged. monitoring window started at 11:56 UTC — will update in 15m.
alexa: :thumbsup: nice quick ops. closing routing change loop once all pending pods are <5 and autoscaler shows healthy decisions.
infra-bot: thread summary: overflow->hosted for dev/staging only, nodes cordoned/drained, incident INC-2024-892 opened, autoscaler hotfix in progress.
